note: Closed value lists for feed contract v2. Each value has a one-line meaning; basis names the doctrine or standard it follows.

values.observation: Something measured or reported, with no judgment about what it means.
values.assessment: A judgment about what is happening now or what it means.
values.forecast: A judgment about what will happen, with a resolution rule Verdict can score.

tier.basis: Grabo; NATO indicators versus indications; JP 2-0 warning

values.anomaly: Measured and outside the baseline. A measurement, not a warning.
values.warning: Judged. Carries likelihood, confidence, alternatives and what would change it.

values.update: Replaces the item named in supersedes.
values.cancel: Withdraws the item named in supersedes.
values.error: Corrects a mistaken issue named in supersedes.

values.exercise: Part of a training range or replay.
values.test: Pipeline test; never shown as live.

human_review.basis: ICD 505 labelling idea, applied to automated output

values.none: Fully automated, rule-based; no person looked at it before release.
values.sampled: A person reviews a sample of items from this method version.
values.full: A person reviewed this item before release.

indicator_state.basis: Grabo; Tom's rule that missing data never means quiet

values.present: The indicator's condition is met in this period.
values.absent: Data arrived and the condition is not met.
values.no_data: Data did not arrive or did not cover enough of the area. Drawn grey; never read as absent.

direction.basis: CIA Tradecraft Primer (2009) indicators and signposts

values.changed: Changed in a way that is not up or down (scope, place, wording).
values.withdrawn: The prior judgment no longer stands.

values.assessed: Reached by this suite's own method from measurements or several independent sources.
values.reported: Reported by an independent outlet or agency; not measured by the suite.
values.claimed: A single-source or party claim. Drawn hollow; never moves a ladder on its own.

values.point: Location as published, to about 1 km.
values.area: A published polygon or the suite's own grid cell.
values.none: No location (for example a software vulnerability). Drawn off-map.

product_category.basis: JP 2-0 intelligence products by purpose, adapted

values.estimative: Estimate or outlook: probabilistic and scored by Verdict.
values.baseline: Baseline or profile page (general military intelligence-like).

us_person_data.basis: A label, not a restriction (Tom, 30 Oct 2026). The programs are not bound by the US intelligence community's limits on US-person information; a consumer that is (for example a government user) filters on this field and strips what its own rules require. US persons are US citizens, permanent residents, US-incorporated companies and associations made up substantially of citizens or permanent residents (FISA, 50 U.S.C. 1801(i); the intelligence community's rules define them the same way in substance).

values.none: Names no person or organization (counts, measurements, places).
values.organizations: Names organizations, which may include US companies or other US organizations.
values.individuals: Names or identifies individuals, who may be US persons (it may name organizations too).

ease_of_faking.basis: Heuer, Psychology of Intelligence Analysis, ch. 8

values.low: Hard to fake (physical measurement from several sensors).
values.medium: Possible to fake with effort (single sensor, official statement).
values.high: Easy to fake (social media post, unverified image, single claim).
